headline: 29 days off: Cabinet approves 2027 public holidays
summary: The government has finalized the holiday list for 2027, though government employees will get 22 actual days off due to weekend overlaps.
details: The Bangladesh cabinet has approved a total of 29 days of public holidays for the year 2027.
The approved list includes 15 general holidays and 14 holidays declared by executive order.
However, since seven of these holidays fall on Fridays and Saturdays, government employees will effectively enjoy 22 days off.
The decision was finalized during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat.
Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani announced the decision during a press conference following the meeting.
caption:
Mark your calendars for 2027! 🗓️ The government has approved 29 public holidays.

The Bangladesh cabinet has approved a total of 29 days of public holidays for the year 2027.

The approved list includes 15 general holidays and 14 holidays declared by executive order.

However, since seven of these holidays fall on Fridays and Saturdays, government employees will effectively enjoy 22 days off.

The decision was finalized during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat.

Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani announced the decision during a press conference following the meeting.

headline: LPG prices surge: 12kg cylinder now Tk 2,060 after monthly hike
summary: The price of private-sector LPG cylinders has jumped by Tk 223 in a single month, contributing to a total increase of Tk 475 over the last two months.
details: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has announced a price hike for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). A 12kg cylinder from the private sector now costs Tk 2,060.
caption:
LPG prices just jumped again. A 12kg cylinder now costs Tk 2,060—a Tk 223 increase in just one month.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has announced a price hike for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). A 12kg cylinder from the private sector now costs Tk 2,060.
